facts.statement: The species was originally described as Sclerorhynchus hiram and later renamed Rhinobatus eretes before being placed in the genus Libanopristis.
facts.quote: synonyms: Sclerorhynchus hiram Hay, 1903 Rhinobatus eretes Hay, 1903

facts.statement: The genus was first described by Hay in 1903.
Libanopristis belongs to the family Sclerorhynchidae.
This animal is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
Libanopristis lived during the Cenomanian stage, between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: This extinct genus lived in Lebanon during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Libanopristis is an extinct genus of ganopristid sclerorhynchoid that lived in Lebanon during the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: A single female specimen containing nine embryos preserved in situ provides early fossil evidence of ovoviviparity in batoids.
facts.quote: One female specimen with nine embryos preserved in situ represents one of the first fossil evidence of batoid ovoviviparity.
